title: Margaritas and Murder at El Paso: The Missing Till
venue: El Paso Mexican Restaurant — Denham Springs
series_title: Margaritas and Murder at El Paso

title_screen.subtitle: A Live Detective Mystery Experience
title_screen.hook: The night begins with a missing till, a broken office camera, and a supervisor who knew too much before closing count.

truth.motive: Ray discovered a cash-skimming pattern before the dinner rush deposits could be corrected
truth.method: Ray was lured into the office and struck during a staged register audit
truth.strongest_evidence: The corrected deposit sheet timestamp matches the bookkeeper's login after Ray was already dead
truth.red_herring: The bartender's loud argument about tips

briefing.host_read: Tonight at El Paso, dinner service turns into a crime scene. The salsa music is still playing, the patio lights are still warm, and every suspect has a reason to protect their own version of the night. Detectives, follow the receipts, the hallway timing, the patio noise, and what the staff tried to clean up before anyone called for help.
briefing.player_prompt: Review each app as clues unlock. Use the round checkpoints to organize what the evidence actually proves. Do not accuse on gossip alone.

clue_theme: cash drawer logs, office hallway movement, corrected receipts, broken camera timing

0.public: Ray Molina is found in the back office after closing count. The register drawer is open, but the missing cash story feels too convenient.

entries.title: Opening Case Note
entries.content: Cash drawer shortage reported at 9:42 PM, but Ray had already flagged a deposit mismatch earlier.

300.public: The office camera failed for seven minutes — exactly during the first story everyone repeats.

entries.title: Office Camera Still
entries.content: Last clean frame shows Ray entering alone at 9:34 PM.

entries.title: Hallway Route
entries.content: Only staff with office access could avoid the dining room cameras.

600.public: A loud argument at the bar may explain tension, but not office access.

entries.title: Bartender Thread
entries.content: Tip argument was public at 9:20 PM and witnessed by three tables.

entries.title: Manager Note
entries.content: Ray said he was checking numbers, not chasing tips.

900.public: The register drawer was opened after Ray was already missing from the floor.

entries.title: Deposit Draft
entries.content: Unsubmitted correction created at 9:51 PM under bookkeeper credentials.

1200.public: The killer needed the theft to look like Ray's mistake.

entries.title: Deposit Comparison
entries.content: Two versions of the same deposit sheet exist. The later one removes a recurring cash discrepancy.

1500.public: Ray was not killed because he stole money. He was killed because he could prove someone else did.

entries.title: Search History
entries.content: how to restore deleted POS correction log

1800.public: Motive, access, and the login timestamp now point in the same direction.

entries.title: Final Evidence
entries.content: Corrected deposit sheet timestamp matches bookkeeper login after Ray's death window.

reveal_copy: The truth points to Bookkeeper. The strongest case is not built on the loudest rumor, but on how motive, method, opportunity, and the evidence trail line up. The detail that closes it: The corrected deposit sheet timestamp matches the bookkeeper's login after Ray was already dead.
